findings.title: Negative offset slicing on a Django queryset raises an error and is reachable by users
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes `cursor.offset` straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when the offset is negative. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. The cursor string is client-controlled (`Cursor.from_string` accepts any int offset), so any user with the flag enabled can trigger a 500. The comment claiming the ORM handles this is wrong. The 'advanced' path also gives no real access to extra data, and the added `max(0, offset)` guard in `BasePaginator` shows the intended behaviour is clamping.

findings.title: Prev-page cursors still pass negative offsets to the queryset
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.get_result`, `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. When `is_prev` is true the raw offset is used, so a negative offset from a crafted cursor reaches the queryset slice and raises. Before this change the same slice was also unguarded, but this edit adds a comment claiming negative offsets are safe. It also changes the shared paginator used by many endpoints without clamping the prev case.

findings.title: Experimental paginator exposed behind a query parameter in the audit log endpoint
findings.body: A user-supplied `optimized_pagination=true` switches the audit log endpoint to a new, untested paginator. The paginator accepts negative offsets, and the gating check is `is_superuser or has_global_access`, which is broad. This adds attack and bug surface to a security-sensitive endpoint. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` also uses `math.floor` on a datetime, which fails because the audit log is ordered by `datetime`, so the optimized path raises a TypeError for the normal `-datetime` ordering.

findings.title: Span count is not tracked correctly before trimming
findings.body: `span_count` comes from the return value of the last `zunionstore`. If neither union branch ran, it falls back to `zcard`. When the span_key union ran, the parent union returned its count only if it also ran. The set can also grow past 1000 between calls because the initial `zadd` happens outside the script. `zpopmin` removes the lowest-score (oldest) spans, so evicting by end timestamp silently drops spans, including possibly the root span payload.

findings.title: The max_segment_spans check was removed but the setting remains
findings.body: The span-count guard in `_load_segment_data` was deleted, so `max_segment_spans` is now unused. It is still accepted by `__init__` and is not included in `__reduce__`, which also omits `segment_page_size` and `max_segment_bytes`, so the settings are lost when the buffer is pickled. The redirect loop limit in the Lua script was also reduced from 10000 to 1000 without justification.

findings.title: end_timestamp_precise is required and read without a fallback
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError for any span payload missing the field, which would crash the whole batch in the consumer. Other fields use `.get()` where optional. A missing score should be handled gracefully.
